author: reek
body: The boot ring gave proc 0 its network scope from the compiler. This is the other door: a signed binary whose approved grant carries a network authority, written into the slot the new process will run under. The verifier always decoded the scope (the format carries it per capability); CapGrant now carries the network scope beside the filesystem one, and apply-load-decision installs it. A binary whose manifest said "network write, to api.example.com" must not arrive able to POST anywhere.

author: reek
body: Two binaries, identical but for the scope literal. The scoped one must arrive scoped; the unscoped one must arrive unscoped, or a loader writing a constant into every slot would pass. The denied load must install NEITHER the bits nor the scope -- writing an untrusted author's authority string into a live slot is the sharpest failure.
